title: Color Temperature Converter
description: Convert light color temperature (Kelvin) to its approximate on-screen color — real blackbody math with warm/cool labels.
howto: Drag the Kelvin slider (or type an exact value) from candlelight 1000K to blue sky 12000K.
See the approximate color as a swatch with HEX and RGB values.
Read the warm / neutral / cool label for lighting and photography reference.

faqs.q: How is Kelvin converted to a color?
faqs.a: With the standard Tanner Helland approximation of blackbody radiation: separate formulas map temperature to red, green and blue channels, clamped to 0–255.
Very close for 2000K–6500K. Above ~8000K the blue channel saturates, so extreme values are indicative rather than exact.
Warm (<3300K: cozy amber light), neutral (3300–5300K: daylight-ish white), cool (>5300K: bluish daylight). Photographers white-balance around these.
